analyst.summary: Tata Steel posted a record FY26 (revenue Rs 2,32,140 crore +6.2%, EBITDA Rs 34,848 crore, PAT ~Rs 10,886 crore +215.6% YoY) driven by a genuinely strong India business (record 23.4mt production, 24% EBITDA margin, newly-commissioned Kalinganagar Phase-2 capacity at 8 MTPA) and real balance-sheet deleveraging (net debt down to Rs 80,144 crore, overseas debt share cut from ~50% to 18%). Unlike prior cycles, this year's improvement traces across quarters rather than a single exceptional item -- a cleaner earnings-quality read. But Europe nets to roughly breakeven (Netherlands turned EBITDA-positive at EUR 267mn, UK stayed loss-making at GBP -217mn), meaning almost all consolidated EBITDA is currently India-sourced at a margin above its historical norm, and two fresh Europe risks -- a Dutch regulatory threat to force early closure of IJmuiden's coke/gas plants, and a further delay to the UK's new electric-arc furnace -- sit on top of an already-incomplete restructuring arc. At ~9x trailing EV/EBITDA and ~21-22x trailing P/E, valuation looks fair rather than cheap once you recognize how concentrated today's profitability is in one cyclically-elevated segment. Hold on an existing position; no thesis break, but not a name to add to blind.
